label: Late original phase / <DEL> after f,z,3,j,e,s,b,q seen
explanation: Fires during input-reading: original-phase steps from t>=2 on, plus the <DEL> step (65% of mass is original phase, 28% is <DEL>; 39% of <DEL> steps fire). Almost silent at t=0-1 and in the copy phase, apart from weak firing on the first one or two outputs. Rate goes up with position (orig_idx 8 fires 58%) and with L. Strongest when the prefix contains f, z, 3, j, e, s, b or q, when the first token is 0/m/i/h, and when the current input is 0 (37% rate). Top examples rise steadily through the sequence and peak on a 0 input or <DEL>. Dev F1 is about 0.48 (precision 0.33, mass recall 0.88). The token dependence is graded and spread across many tokens, so precision stays low: it looks like a direction in the hidden state built from content, not a clean token rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: f, 3, z, e, q, s; least: d, u, i, -) and the input two steps back (most: z, f, 3, e, s, b; least: u, w, i, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=8, L=8 & t=9, L=3 & t=1.
